myths.title: Icarus and the Sun
myths.summary: A son ignores his father's warning and flies too close to the sun on wax wings.

myths.title: Prometheus Steals Fire
myths.summary: A titan steals fire from the gods and gives it to humanity, and pays a steep price.

myths.title: Sisyphus and the Boulder
myths.summary: A king is condemned to push a boulder uphill for eternity, watching it roll back each time.

myths.title: Pandora's Box
myths.summary: Curiosity leads to a container of the world's ills being opened despite a warning.

myths.title: The Trojan Horse
myths.summary: A gift conceals an army; trust in appearances leads to a city's downfall.

myths.title: King Midas's Golden Touch
myths.summary: A king is granted a wish that turns everything he touches to gold, including what he loves.

myths.title: Theseus and the Labyrinth
myths.summary: A hero navigates a monster-filled maze using a single thread to find his way back out.

myths.title: The Phoenix
myths.summary: A mythical bird periodically dies in flame and is reborn from its own ashes.

myths.title: Orpheus and Eurydice
myths.summary: A musician is allowed to lead his love out of the underworld on one condition -- don't look back -- and looks back too soon.

myths.title: Achilles' Heel
myths.summary: A warrior made invulnerable everywhere except the one spot his mother held him by, which is exactly where he is struck.

myths.title: Narcissus and His Reflection
myths.summary: A beautiful youth falls hopelessly in love with his own reflection in a pool and cannot look away.

myths.title: Persephone and the Pomegranate
myths.summary: Eating a few seeds from the underworld binds a goddess to return there every year, creating the seasons.

myths.title: Atlas Holding Up the Sky
myths.summary: A titan is condemned to bear the weight of the heavens on his shoulders forever as punishment.

myths.title: Cassandra's Curse
myths.summary: A prophet is granted the gift of true prophecy and the curse that no one will ever believe her.

myths.title: Daedalus and the Labyrinth
myths.summary: A brilliant craftsman builds a maze so effective that even he becomes trapped by his own creation.

myths.title: Odysseus and the Sirens
myths.summary: A captain has himself bound to the mast so he can hear a deadly, irresistible song without steering his ship into the rocks.

myths.title: Tantalus's Eternal Hunger
myths.summary: A king is punished by standing in water beneath fruit he can never quite reach, forever almost satisfied.

myths.title: Medusa's Gaze
myths.summary: A gorgon's stare turns any onlooker instantly to stone, so she is only ever defeated by someone who refuses to look directly at her.

myths.title: Arachne the Weaver
myths.summary: A weaver so proud of her skill that she challenges a goddess to a contest, and is transformed into a spider for her hubris.

myths.title: Hercules and the Hydra
myths.summary: A hero fights a serpent where cutting off one head causes two more to grow back in its place.

myths.title: The Augean Stables
myths.summary: A hero is given an impossibly filthy, decades-old task and solves it not with brute force but by rerouting two entire rivers.

myths.title: Loki Bound
myths.summary: A trickster god's endless schemes finally catch up with him, and he is chained in place as punishment for one deception too many.

myths.title: Ragnarok
myths.summary: A foretold, inevitable end of the world arrives exactly as prophesied, and from its ruin a new world eventually rises.

myths.title: Odin's Eye for Wisdom
myths.summary: A god trades one of his own eyes for a single drink from the well of all knowledge and wisdom.

myths.title: Osiris Dismembered and Restored
myths.summary: A god is torn into pieces scattered across the land, then painstakingly gathered and reassembled to be made whole again.

myths.title: Yu the Great Tames the Flood
myths.summary: Where his father failed by building walls to block a great flood, a son succeeds by patiently carving channels to guide the water instead.

myths.title: The Ouroboros
myths.summary: A serpent eternally consumes its own tail, forming an endless, self-sustaining, self-referential cycle.

myths.title: Procrustes' Bed
myths.summary: A host forces every traveler to fit one exact bed, stretching the short and cutting down the tall until they match.

myths.title: The Gordian Knot
myths.summary: An impossibly tangled knot that no one can untie is finally undone -- by simply cutting straight through it.

myths.title: The Sword of Damocles
myths.summary: A guest is seated beneath a sword hanging by a single thread, meant to show how fragile comfort is at the top.

tech_trivia.title: The `yes` command
tech_trivia.detail: A Unix utility whose only job is to print 'y' forever until killed — used to auto-confirm prompts.

tech_trivia.title: Byzantine Generals Problem
tech_trivia.detail: A distributed-systems thought experiment about reaching consensus when some nodes may lie.

tech_trivia.title: The Year 2000 Problem
tech_trivia.detail: Two-digit year storage meant systems risked treating 2000 as 1900.

tech_trivia.title: Core dumps
tech_trivia.detail: Named after magnetic core memory; a crashed process's memory snapshot written to disk.

tech_trivia.title: The CAP Theorem
tech_trivia.detail: A distributed database can only guarantee two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.

tech_trivia.title: Bit rot
tech_trivia.detail: The gradual, unintended corruption of stored data over time due to physical media decay or neglect.

tech_trivia.title: Thundering herd problem
tech_trivia.detail: Many processes wake and compete for a single resource at once, overwhelming the system that just freed it.

tech_trivia.title: Cache invalidation
tech_trivia.detail: Famously one of the two hardest problems in computer science: knowing when cached data is stale.

tech_trivia.title: Race condition
tech_trivia.detail: A bug where the outcome depends on the unpredictable timing of two processes, so it can pass a hundred tests and fail on the hundred-and-first.

tech_trivia.title: The Dining Philosophers Problem
tech_trivia.detail: A classic illustration of deadlock: five philosophers, five forks, and every philosopher waiting on a neighbor who is also waiting.

tech_trivia.title: Rubber duck debugging
tech_trivia.detail: The practice of explaining your code line by line to an inanimate object -- often a rubber duck -- until the bug becomes obvious to you.

tech_trivia.title: Heisenbug
tech_trivia.detail: A bug that seems to change or vanish the moment you try to observe or debug it -- named as a nod to the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

tech_trivia.title: Off-by-one error
tech_trivia.detail: One of the most common bugs in programming: a loop or index that runs one time too many, or one time too few.

tech_trivia.title: Memory leak
tech_trivia.detail: Memory that a program allocates but never releases, slowly starving the system of resources the longer the program runs.

tech_trivia.title: The null reference
tech_trivia.detail: Called 'my billion-dollar mistake' by its own inventor, Tony Hoare, for the sheer number of crashes it has caused since 1965.

tech_trivia.title: Spaghetti code
tech_trivia.detail: Code with so many tangled, criss-crossing paths of logic that following any single thread through it is nearly impossible.

tech_trivia.title: Cosmic ray bit flips
tech_trivia.detail: A high-energy particle from space can occasionally strike a memory chip and flip a single bit, causing an error with no software cause at all.

tech_trivia.title: Cold start latency
tech_trivia.detail: The extra delay a serverless function incurs the first time it runs after being idle, before its environment is warmed up.

tech_trivia.title: The Two Generals Problem
tech_trivia.detail: A proof that two parties can never be perfectly certain they agree on a plan when their only communication channel might lose messages.

tech_trivia.title: Conway's Law
tech_trivia.detail: Organizations design systems that mirror their own communication structure -- the org chart quietly becomes the architecture diagram.

tech_trivia.title: Brooks's Law
tech_trivia.detail: Adding more people to an already-late software project tends to make it later still, not faster.

tech_trivia.title: The Ninety-Ninety Rule
tech_trivia.detail: The first 90% of a project takes 90% of the time, and the remaining 10% takes the other 90% of the time.

tech_trivia.title: Technical debt
tech_trivia.detail: A shortcut taken now to ship faster, which quietly accrues interest until it eventually has to be paid back with real engineering time.

tech_trivia.title: The leap second
tech_trivia.detail: An occasional extra second inserted into official time to keep clocks aligned with Earth's rotation -- and a recurring source of production outages.

tech_trivia.title: Deadlock
tech_trivia.detail: A state where two or more processes each hold a resource the other needs, and neither can ever proceed.

tech_trivia.title: Zero-day vulnerability
tech_trivia.detail: A security flaw discovered and potentially exploited before the people who could fix it have had a single day to patch it.

tech_trivia.title: Hash collision
tech_trivia.detail: When two completely different inputs produce the exact same hash output, undermining the assumption that a hash uniquely identifies its data.

tech_trivia.title: Moore's Law
tech_trivia.detail: The observation that the number of transistors on a chip tends to double roughly every two years, driving decades of exponential hardware progress.

tech_trivia.title: Dead code
tech_trivia.detail: Code that still exists in the codebase but can never actually be reached or executed by any path the program takes.

tech_trivia.title: Magic number
tech_trivia.detail: An unexplained numeric literal buried directly in code, with no name or comment to tell future readers what it actually means.
